Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and G922; weightless, i.e. (figuratively) not burdensome:--from being burdensome.
BiblicalUsage: This Greek word for 'not burdensome' occurs once, in 2 Corinthians 11:9: 'when I was present with you, and wanted, I was chargeable to no man.' Paul is defending his ministry — he worked with his own hands and let the Macedonians supply his need rather than burden the Corinthians.
TheologicalSignificance: One verse shows me Paul’s heart for the churches — he would rather go without than be a weight on the people he served — and it makes me check whether my own service lightens anyone’s load or adds to it.
